subject: VAL
label: Grade 09
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 09 Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Values and character
modules.outcome: describe values and how they guide choices
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Values and character', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: describe values and how they guide choices. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Values and character' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: describe values and how they guide choices. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: Empathy steps: notice, ask, listen, say back what you heard, offer help. After a mistake: what happened, what I learned, what I will do next. Method: Model run for 'Values and character'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Describe values and how they guide choices: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Values and character), and at which Bloom level is it?
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Digital ethics) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: kindness, honesty and sharing in daily life.
L2: responsibility, courage and care for others and nature.
L3: fairness, respect for difference and service.
L5: leadership, wellbeing and ethical reasoning.
L6 (degree): applied ethics, culture and community work.
L7 (postgraduate): scholarship, counselling or teaching at depth.
